sentences.zh: 五十六年秋，昭襄王卒，子孝文王立。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifty-sixth year, King Zhaoxiang died, and his son King Xiaowen was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifty-sixth year, King Zhaoxiang died, and his son King Xiaowen took the throne.

sentences.zh: 尊唐八子為唐太后，而合其葬於先王。

translations.literal: They honored Lady Tang, an Eight-rank Consort, as Empress Dowager Tang and joined her burial with that of the former king.
translations.idiomatic: They honored Lady Tang, an Eight-rank Consort, as Empress Dowager Tang and buried her together with the former king.

sentences.zh: 韓王衰绖入弔祠，諸侯皆使其將相來弔祠，視喪事。

translations.literal: The King of Han came in mourning garments to offer condolences and sacrifices. The feudal lords all sent their generals and chancellors to offer condolences and sacrifices and to observe the funeral arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Han came in mourning dress to offer condolences and sacrifices. The feudal lords all sent generals and chancellors to do the same and to observe the funeral arrangements.

sentences.zh: 孝文王元年，赦罪人，修先王功臣，褒厚親戚，弛苑囿。

translations.literal: In King Xiaowen’s first year, he pardoned criminals, honored the meritorious ministers of the former kings, richly rewarded his relatives, and relaxed the restrictions on parks and preserves.
translations.idiomatic: In King Xiaowen’s first year, he pardoned criminals, honored the former kings’ meritorious ministers, richly rewarded his relatives, and loosened restrictions on parks and preserves.

sentences.zh: 孝文王除喪，十月己亥即位，三日辛醜卒，子莊襄王立。

translations.literal: After King Xiaowen completed mourning, he ascended the throne on the jihai day of the tenth month. Three days later, on the xinchou day, he died, and his son King Zhuangxiang was established.
translations.idiomatic: After King Xiaowen completed mourning, he ascended the throne on the jihai day of the tenth month. Three days later, on the xinchou day, he died, and his son King Zhuangxiang took the throne.

sentences.zh: 莊襄王元年，大赦罪人，修先王功臣，施德厚骨肉而布惠於民。

translations.literal: In King Zhuangxiang’s first year, he granted a general amnesty to criminals, honored the meritorious ministers of the former kings, showed generous virtue to his close kin, and spread favor among the people.
translations.idiomatic: In King Zhuangxiang’s first year, he granted a general amnesty to criminals, honored the former kings’ meritorious ministers, showed generous favor to his close kin, and extended grace to the people.

sentences.zh: 東周君與諸侯謀秦，秦使相國呂不韋誅之，盡入其國。

translations.literal: The Lord of Eastern Zhou plotted with the feudal lords against Qin. Qin sent Chancellor Lü Buwei to execute him and took all his territory into Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The Lord of Eastern Zhou plotted against Qin with the feudal lords. Qin sent Chancellor Lü Buwei to execute him and absorbed all his territory.

sentences.zh: 秦不絕其祀，以陽人地賜周君，奉其祭祀。

translations.literal: Qin did not cut off his sacrifices. It granted the Lord of Zhou land at Yangren to maintain his sacrificial rites.
translations.idiomatic: Qin did not sever his sacrifices; it granted the Lord of Zhou land at Yangren to maintain his rites.

sentences.zh: 使蒙驁伐韓，韓獻成皋、鞏。

translations.literal: He had Meng Ao attack Han. Han offered Chenggao and Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Meng Ao to attack Han. Han offered Chenggao and Gong.

sentences.zh: 秦界至大梁，初置三川郡。

translations.literal: Qin’s boundary reached Daliang, and Sanchuan Commandery was first established.
translations.idiomatic: Qin’s border reached Daliang, and Sanchuan Commandery was established for the first time.

sentences.zh: 二年，使蒙驁攻趙，定太原。

translations.literal: In the second year, he sent Meng Ao to attack Zhao and pacify Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, he sent Meng Ao to attack Zhao and bring Taiyuan under control.

sentences.zh: 三年，蒙驁攻魏高都、汲，拔之。

translations.literal: In the third year, Meng Ao attacked Wei's Gaodu and Ji and seized them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Meng Ao attacked Wei’s Gaodu and Ji and captured them.

sentences.zh: 攻趙榆次、新城、狼孟，取三十七城。

translations.literal: They attacked Zhao's Yuci, Xincheng, and Langmeng, taking thirty-seven cities.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked Zhao’s Yuci, Xincheng, and Langmeng, capturing thirty-seven cities.

sentences.zh: 四月日食。

translations.literal: Fourth month solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: （四年）

translations.literal: (fourth year)
translations.idiomatic: (Fourth year of the reign.)

sentences.zh: 王龁攻上黨。

translations.literal: Wang He attacked Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang He attacked Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 初置太原郡。

translations.literal: Taiyuan Commandery was first established.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan Commandery was first established.

sentences.zh: 魏將無忌率五國兵擊秦，秦卻於河外。

translations.literal: The Wei general Wuji led troops from five states to attack Qin. Qin retreated beyond the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei general Wuji led troops from five states in an attack on Qin, forcing Qin back beyond the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 蒙驁敗，解而去。

translations.literal: Meng Ao was defeated, lifted the siege, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Ao was defeated, raised the siege, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 五月丙午，莊襄王卒，子政立，是為秦始皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the bingwu day, King Zhuangxiang died. His son Zheng was established; this was the First Emperor of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the bingwu day, King Zhuangxiang died. His son Zheng took the throne; this was the First Emperor of Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦王政立二十六年，初并天下為三十六郡，號為始皇帝。

translations.literal: King Zheng of Qin had reigned for twenty-six years when he first united all under heaven into thirty-six commanderies and took the title First Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: King Zheng of Qin had reigned for twenty-six years when he first unified all under heaven into thirty-six commanderies and took the title First Emperor.

sentences.zh: 始皇帝五十一年而崩，子胡亥立，是為二世皇帝。

translations.literal: The First Emperor died in his fifty-first year. His son Huhai was established; this was the Second Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor died at the age of fifty-one. His son Huhai took the throne as the Second Emperor.

sentences.zh: 三年，諸侯并起叛秦，趙高殺二世，立子嬰。

translations.literal: In the third year, the feudal lords rose together and rebelled against Qin. Zhao Gao killed the Second Emperor and established Ziying.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, the feudal lords rose together in rebellion against Qin. Zhao Gao killed the Second Emperor and installed Ziying.

sentences.zh: 子嬰立月餘，諸侯誅之，遂滅秦。

translations.literal: Ziying had been established for more than a month when the feudal lords executed him and then extinguished Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Ziying had held power for a little over a month when the feudal lords executed him and brought Qin to an end.

sentences.zh: 其語在始皇本紀中。

translations.literal: The account of this appears in the Basic Annals of the First Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: This account appears in the Basic Annals of the First Emperor.

sentences.zh: 太史公曰：秦之先為嬴姓。

translations.literal: The Grand Historian said: Qin's ancestors bore the surname Ying.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Historian says: Qin’s ancestors bore the surname Ying.

sentences.zh: 其後分封，以國為姓，有徐氏、郯氏、莒氏、終黎氏、運奄氏、菟裘氏、將梁氏、黃氏、江氏、修魚氏、白冥氏、蜚廉氏、秦氏。

translations.literal: Afterward, when the descendants were divided and enfeoffed, they took their states as surnames: Xu, Tan, Ju, Zhongli, Yunyan, Tuqiu, Jiangliang, Huang, Jiang, Xiuyu, Baiming, Feilian, and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when their descendants were divided and enfeoffed, they took state names as surnames: Xu, Tan, Ju, Zhongli, Yunyan, Tuqiu, Jiangliang, Huang, Jiang, Xiuyu, Baiming, Feilian, and Qin.

sentences.zh: 然秦以其先造父封趙城，為趙氏。

translations.literal: Yet because Qin’s ancestor Zaofu had been enfeoffed at Zhaocheng, they became the Zhao clan.
translations.idiomatic: However, because Qin’s ancestor Zaofu had been enfeoffed at Zhaocheng, they became the Zhao clan.
